title: Safety-guided KV autotuner and key ontology for cost-aware caching
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: Goal: deliver an automated recommendation and safe-apply system that proposes per-prefix/per-key TTLs, batching knobs, and cache-key reshaping suggestions with a probabilistic hit-rate model and gated rollout controls. The feature should reduce token cost for common workloads by ~10–30% without increasing tail latency or error surface. This ticket covers modeling, recommendation heuristics, safety gates (shadow/gradual apply/auto-rollback), and a minimal console integration to present suggested changes and explain expected cost/latency trade-offs.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation engine produces TTL + batching suggestions for >= 80% of active prefixes in sample workloads
Automated safety gates (shadow apply, canary cohort, metric-based rollback) are implemented and exercised in staging
A/B test on two customer-like workloads shows token-cost reduction >= 8% with no >5% increase in 95th pct latency
Console shows human-readable rationale per suggestion (hit-rate delta, expected token-savings, risk tag)
Playbook for rollback and emergency revert is documented and linked from the UI
tasks: Build hit-rate forecasting model (sampled prefix histograms + Bayesian smoothing)
Implement TTL annealing policy generator with confidence bands
Design key-ontology transform rules: affix normalization, length bucketing, and canonicalization heuristics
Add shadow-apply pipeline to run candidate policy without affecting production cache (metrics only)
Create canary cohort rollout: cohort selection, staged apply throttler, and automatic rollback thresholds
Console integration: suggestion UI, explanation text, runbook link, and apply button (disabled unless safety checks pass)
E2E tests: synthetic trace replay harness + load tests to validate cost/latency impact
Instrument metrics and alerts: per-prefix hitrate, eviction delta, token-cost delta, tail-latency, error-rate
progress_notes: 2025-02-18: Kickoff — scoped ML model type (Poisson-Binomial with Bayesian priors) and initial datasets (7 days sampled traces). Priya leading modeling work.
2025-02-25: Prototype hit-rate estimator (histogram smoothing) returns stable estimates for prefixes >100 queries/day; noisy under 10/day — Rafael to add low-volume fallback heuristics.
2025-02-28: Spike shows TTL annealing in 3 steps (10x -> 3x -> 1.5x) provides safe savings; need to formalize confidence bands for each anneal step.
2025-03-03: Safety design review — agreed on shadow apply + two-stage canary + metric-based auto-rollback. PM asked for clear customer-facing explanation strings.
2025-03-04: Integration work started on console hooks; UX will show ‘expected savings’ and ‘risk score’ per suggestion (Rafael).
decisions: Use sampled prefix histograms and Bayesian smoothing rather than heavy per-request ML to keep the recommendation engine lightweight and explainable
TTL recommendations will be expressed as discrete anneal steps (coarse-grained) to minimize oscillation and avoid churning cache contents
Cache-key ontology changes will be proposed as non-destructive canonicalization (e.g., trim tracking params, normalize timestamps) and flagged as opt-in
Rollout safety uses three controls: shadow apply (non-destructive), canary cohorts (1%, 10%, 50%), and metric thresholds that auto-revert (token-cost or latency regressions)
risk_and_mitigations: Risk: Over-aggressive TTLs could increase upstream load and tail latency. Mitigation: conservative confidence bands + staged anneal + rollback triggers based on 95p latency and error-rate
Risk: Low-volume prefixes produce noisy forecasts and bad autosuggestions. Mitigation: fallback to safe defaults and flag low-confidence suggestions for manual review
Risk: Canonicalization could collide keys across tenants. Mitigation: add tenant-scoped collision checks and an opt-in preview mode before apply
Risk: Black-box suggestions reduce operator trust. Mitigation: include per-suggestion rationale, counterfactual estimates, and a simulation mode in the console
metrics_and_thresholds: Primary metric: token-cost delta (target >= -10% for treated traffic)
Safety metrics: 95th pct latency change (<+5% allowed during canary), error-rate delta (<+1% absolute), eviction-rate increase (<+20% relative)
Hitrate uplift target per-prefix >= +8% for prefixes with >100 QPS equivalent traffic
Auto-rollback triggers: token-cost regression >+3% or 95p latency regression >+7% sustained for 5 minutes
rollout_plan: Stage 0 (staging): shadow-run candidate policies on sampled traffic and validate metrics (2 days)
Stage 1 (canary-1): apply to 1% cohort for 6 hours, monitor, and wait for stability window
Stage 2 (canary-10): expand to 10% for 24 hours if canary-1 passes
Stage 3 (gradual roll): 50% -> 100% with progressive anneal steps and periodic validations
Immediate abort: if auto-rollback triggers fire, revert to previous policy and open incident ticket
testing_plan: Synthetic trace replay using historical prefix traces (7-day and 28-day windows)
Load tests with spike scenarios to check eviction churn and tail-latency under burst
Shadow-canary k6 harness to validate shadow-apply correctness and metric integrity
Manual validation checklist for on-call: verify per-prefix hitrate, check top-10 changed prefixes, confirm no cross-tenant key collisions
